modalCorrections.MCCCOMM311: Persuasive Communication builds on classical rhetoric and argumentation to study persuasion in science, society and sustainability. Students examine framing, nudging, cognitive shortcuts and ethical approaches to persuasion. In a community-engaged project, they help local institutions address communication challenges.
modalCorrections.MCCMEDI111: Introduction to Film & Media focuses primarily on cinema history, film culture and analysis. Students study narrative, cinematography, editing and sound, examine influential films in their theoretical and political contexts, and engage with academic readings. The final part briefly connects film to television, streaming and digital platforms.

courseReview.advisoryProgression: Closest rhetoric precedes persuasion. Political option places rhetoric and advanced persuasion together in semester3; no formal prerequisite fails, but earlier rhetoric is preferable if this concept is ultimately retained. Digital option provides actual business/methods/marketing before strategy/market research. Social Theory assumes introductory/modern sociology; political option omits Modern Sociology, an advisory matter to reconsider in a source-resolved final concept, not a new hard prerequisite.
